objective: Provide operational evidence and proposed criteria for a small-rank, one-node Rouaix CPU P0; no solver changes or scientific gate decision.
decision_for_32_gib: Not justified as a safe production request from existing evidence. A 32-GiB request could be used only as an explicitly bounded memory-qualification trial after confirming site enforcement and a usable aggregate-memory measurement. Otherwise use 64 GiB for a performance baseline.

assumptions.statement: The proposed 24-rank case reuses the existing clean-start mesh and original numerical variant, with only the rank count/decomposition and resource request changed.
assumptions.basis: Primary task description; candidate settings are proposed, not measured.

assumptions.statement: The two rank-inverse wall estimates assume fixed per-cell/per-step cost and no change in convergence, memory pressure, network placement, or output behavior.
assumptions.basis: Back-of-envelope operational extrapolation only; not a fit and not evidence that a 5 s run is affordable.

assumptions.statement: A 20 percent margin below a 32-GiB request (25.6 GiB aggregate high-water bound) is proposed as conservative operational headroom if a 32-GiB qualification gate is needed.
assumptions.basis: Agent-proposed resource margin; not paper-derived or established by prior runs.

proposed_gate_criteria.queue_fit: Take a fresh Slurm snapshot and require at least 24 idle CPU cores on one eligible cpu-partition node. At 14:43:49Z the largest fragment was 16, so this P0 was not currently placeable as one node.
proposed_gate_criteria.memory_32_gib: Do not sign off 32 GiB from current evidence. A qualification trial must confirm site memory enforcement semantics and capture step aggregate memory. Proposed conservative pass criterion: sum of task high-water RSS no greater than 25.6 GiB through the final write, plus no memory failure; if aggregate data or enforcement semantics are unavailable, mark unqualified. Otherwise request 64 GiB for forward-progress work.
proposed_gate_criteria.runtime: 60-minute Slurm wall cap is a bounded P0; the two unfitted estimates are about 27-32 minutes for 100 steps. Stop on solver failure, non-finite state, no declared progress, or wall cap; preserve failure and do not change deltaT or solver constants.
proposed_gate_criteria.completion: Require clean-start solver exit 0, time 0.01 s reached, exactly 100 fixed steps, scheduled final write captured, compact ledger audit and solver convergence checks recorded. Exploratory completion is not an E1 validation pass.
proposed_gate_criteria.performance_report: Report solver_wall_s, logged time window, steps, allocated core-hours, measured CPU time, per-rank cell-step rate, memory accounting rows, node placement, output bytes, and pressure-profile max/average/min if profiled. Do not call this rank count optimal from one run.
proposed_gate_criteria.5_s_progression: Do not project a 5 s budget from this 0.01 s P0 alone. The existing progression contract uses a longer completed window (0.25-0.49 s for a 0.5 s run) and checks storage, output and deadline first.

profiling_pair.profiled_change_only: Add the native profiling controlDict block documented in docs/HPC_RUN_METRICS.md:340-347; freeze a separate case hash. This is the only prepared-case file difference; numerical settings remain identical.

The 24-rank 0.01 s pilot cannot establish a stable longer-horizon throughput forecast or E1 scientific validity.
